## Canopy in brief

- What it is: a layer above Git (not a Git replacement) for repositories where many AI coding agents work in parallel, each in its own worktree.
- What it does: records what each agent reads and writes via harness hooks; notifies an agent in its next tool call when another agent changes a function it read or calls; lets `main` move only through `canopy land`, which runs sandboxed checks on the exact merge commit and attaches an Ed25519-signed record as a Git note; a `pre-receive` hook refuses any other route into `main`.
- Works with: Claude Code today (HTTP hooks). Node 22.13+, Git 2.38+, no npm dependencies. macOS tested; Linux sandbox untested.
- Status: v0.1. 93 of 93 tests pass with scripted agents. Not yet security-tested by a third party and not yet run at length with real agents.
- Measured: hook round trip p50 0.46 ms; semantic conflict reported 22 ms after the edit; about 0.6 s fixed cost per landing; default setting is slower than a plain serial merge queue for unrelated branches (12.2 s vs 9.2 s for eight), `disjoint` setting is faster (5.9 s).
- Try it: `git clone {{github}}/canopy && cd canopy && node bin/canopy.mjs demo`
